privacyPolicy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how {{name}} collects, uses, and protects your information when you use this app.

collect.title: 1. Information We Collect
collect.body: We collect information you provide directly — name, email, phone number, reservation details, service requests, activity bookings, and feedback — as well as basic device information needed to operate the app securely.

use.title: 2. How We Use Your Information
use.body: Your information is used to manage your reservation, fulfil service and activity requests, respond to feedback, personalize recommendations (such as activities matching your interests), and communicate important updates about your stay.

visibility.title: 3. Who Can See Your Information
visibility.body: Reservation and request details are visible to authorized hotel staff and management involved in fulfilling them. We do not sell your personal information to third parties.

security.title: 4. Data Storage & Security
security.body: Your data is stored with industry-standard security controls, including role-based access so only staff with a legitimate need can view guest information.

choices.title: 5. Your Choices
choices.body: You can review and update your personal details at any time in Profile → Personal Details. You may also adjust marketing and personalization preferences in Profile → Privacy.

retention.title: 6. Data Retention
retention.body: We retain reservation and stay history to provide loyalty benefits and past-stay records. You may request deletion of your account data by contacting us using the details below, subject to legal and accounting retention requirements.

contact.title: 7. Contact
contact.body: Privacy questions or requests can be directed to {{email}} or {{phone}}, {{address}}.

privacySettings.footnote: For details on what data we collect and how it's used, see our Privacy Policy in Profile → Privacy Policy.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These Terms of Service govern your use of the {{name}} guest app. Please read them carefully.

acceptance.title: 1. Acceptance of Terms
acceptance.body: By creating an account or using the {{name}} app, you agree to these Terms of Service. If you do not agree, please do not use the app.

reservations.title: 2. Reservations & Check-In
reservations.body: Reservations made through this app are subject to availability and the rate policies communicated at the time of booking. Digital check-in is offered as a convenience and does not replace identity verification at the front desk where required by law.

serviceRequests.title: 3. Service Requests & Activities
serviceRequests.body: Service requests, activity bookings, and dining reservations submitted through the app are fulfilled on a best-effort basis and may be subject to capacity, weather, or operational constraints. We will notify you as soon as possible of any changes.

conduct.title: 4. Guest Conduct
conduct.body: You agree to use the app only for lawful purposes connected with your stay, and not to submit false, abusive, or harassing content through service requests, feedback, or concierge messaging.

cancellations.title: 5. Cancellations
cancellations.body: Cancellation terms for reservations, activities, and dining follow the policy stated at the time of booking. Where no policy is stated, standard hotel cancellation terms apply — ask our front desk or concierge for details.

liability.title: 6. Limitation of Liability
liability.body: {{name}} is not liable for indirect or consequential loss arising from use of this app, including service interruptions, third-party excursion providers, or inaccuracies in third-party information (such as local event listings) presented for your convenience.

changes.title: 7. Changes to These Terms
changes.body: We may update these Terms from time to time. Continued use of the app after changes take effect constitutes acceptance of the revised Terms.

contact.title: 8. Contact
contact.body: Questions about these Terms can be directed to {{email}} or {{phone}}.

trailMaps.title: Trail Maps
trailMaps.offlineNotice: Works fully offline — no signal needed on the trail.
trailMaps.intro: Bundled guides for exploring on foot, from the capital to the island's long-distance trail network.
trailMaps.roseauDesc: Dominica's compact capital is easily walkable — French colonial architecture along Old Street and King George V Street, the Old Market Square, the Bayfront promenade, and the Roseau Cathedral, all within about a 20-minute walk of each other.
trailMaps.waitukubuliSubtitle: The Caribbean's first long-distance trail — 14 segments, about 184 km end to end.
trailMaps.passNotice: All visitors need a Trail Pass to hike any segment of the Waitukubuli National Trail — available at ports of entry, the Forestry, Wildlife & Parks Division, and vendors near trail segments. Hikers are urged to register before setting out and to exercise caution, especially on the very difficult segments.
trailMaps.footnote: Carry water, sun protection, and sturdy footwear — mobile signal is unreliable on most segments.

s1.name: Segment 1
s1.route: Scotts Head Village to Soufriere Estate
s1.desc: The trail's toughest and most iconic opening stretch, crossing a volcanic sulphur-deposit crater with rope-assisted climbing and gorge walking. Passes Toloulou Valley, Crabier Plateau, Bois Cotiette Estate, Sulphur Springs, the Soufriere-Scotts Head Marine Reserve, Morne Kwabier Plateau, and a historic coffee estate.

s2.name: Segment 2
s2.desc: Traces the Old Slave Route past the Soufriere Sulphur Springs and an old agricultural station, through small farms and grazing land on the way into thick rainforest. Also passes Tarish Picnic Park, linking Dominica's natural wonders with its Maroon and colonial history.

s3.name: Segment 3
s3.desc: Enters Morne Trois Pitons National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with a side loop toward Boiling Lake and a stop at Giraudel Botanic Gardens. Passes organic tea plots, the Giraudel community, River Clair, and warm sulphur pools, with aerial views over Roseau.

s4.name: Segment 4
s4.desc: Cuts through the heart of Morne Trois Pitons National Park with views of five mountains across primary and secondary forest, passing the Wotten Waven hot spas, Morne Jack, and the Middleham Falls trail, plus vistas over Freshwater Lake and the Valley of Desolation. Ends at the trail's Research and Interpretation Facility at Pont Casse.

s5.name: Segment 5
s5.desc: Follows the historic Old Carib Trace (Kalinago Stone Pathway) past the Emerald Pool, Jaco Cave, and Savanne David, through the small community of Fond Melle, to the Atlantic coast at Castle Bruce. Also passes Castle Bruce Swamp, Creole Gardens, and the L'Or River.

s6.name: Segment 6
s6.desc: Enters the Kalinago Territory, home to Dominica's Indigenous Kalinago people, passing the Kalinago Barana Aute cultural village, Isulakati Waterfall, and stunning Atlantic coastline views, plus L'Escalier Tete Chien and Horseback Ridge.

s7.name: Segment 7
s7.route: Hatton Garden to First Camp (Heights of Marigot)
s7.desc: An introduction to Dominica's agricultural heartland, crossing cultivated farmland and primary forest between rivers and coastal vistas. Passes Congorie Hole and Walter Williams Orchard — a noted parrot habitat and birdwatching spot with its own birding tower — with views over the northeast coast and Melville Hall Airport.

s8.name: Segment 8
s8.route: Melville Hall Estate (First Camp) to Petite Macoucherie
s8.desc: One of the trail's hardest and longest days, crossing the Northern Forest Reserve, fording rivers, and climbing over Mosquito Mountain before descending to Carholm Estate — especially demanding in wet weather. Rewards with coastal views both east and west, swimmable river pools, and a chance to spot the Sisserou Parrot, Dominica's national bird.

s9.name: Segment 9
s9.desc: A banana-farm access road gives way to the Northern Forest Reserve for a relentless up-and-down 'roller coaster' through mixed farmland and virgin forest, ending in the highlands above Colihaut Village. Passes the island's largest Gommier tree, Kachibona Lake, and Morne Amery.

s10.name: Segment 10
s10.desc: The trail's westernmost and easiest segment, following old and abandoned farm and estate roads through heavily forested terrain in the Northern Forest Reserve, with good odds of spotting both the Jaco and Sisserou Parrots. Passes panoramic views of the north coast and Morne Diablotin, ending at the Syndicate Nature Trail's reception centre.

s11.name: Segment 11
s11.desc: Crosses the north-central highlands through Morne Diablotin National Park, Dominica's largest protected area, past parrot habitat, wild rivers, and the island's only old railway line. Passes Dubam Falls and a parrot reserve, with horseback riding and an agricultural station near Portsmouth, and camping available at Ross Castle and Syndicate.

s12.name: Segment 12
s12.desc: Runs through Vieille Case (Itassi Village) along the rugged Atlantic coast, mixing dry forest, farmland, and old estate roads. Passes views of Portsmouth and Cabrits and Morne Aux Diables — an area used as a filming location for Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest — opening up rarely visited rural communities.

s13.name: Segment 13
s13.desc: Dominica's driest trail section, crossing volcanic terrain and dry forest woodland along the north coast. Passes Lost Grand Fond Village, Tafia Falls, and viewpoints toward the French islands of Marie-Galante, the Saintes, and Guadeloupe, ending at Canna Heritage Park in Capuchin.

s14.name: Segment 14
s14.route: Capuchin to Cabrits National Park (Fort Shirley)
s14.desc: The trail's final stretch, passing the coastal villages of Toucarie, Cottage, Clifton, and Tanetane, with stops at Bell Hall Beach and Toucarie Beach, traditional fishing boats, and bay-oil and cassava processing sites, before finishing at Fort Shirley within Cabrits National Park.
